text:
Jack McBain plays the game the way his 6'4", 219-pound frame suggests. He has 86 hits in 22 games while playing 12.8 minutes a night, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his line leans on dump-ins and the forecheck: he carries the puck in on only 19% of his entries.

He has found the net lately, with goals against Vegas on Nov. 11 and San Jose on Nov. 14. On the season he has 3 goals on 4.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), so he is a goal or two light, and his last ten games produced 4 points against the 3.5 we'd expect. Nothing here is running hot.

The five-on-five results are good this season: Utah takes 57.4% of the expected goals with him on the ice. That is a turn from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.14 more expected goals per 60 with him out there (bottom 10% of forwards) and rated him around replacement level.

The same tracking gives him a strength people miss: 71% of his exits leave the zone with possession. Watch whether that keeps his line out of its own end as his minutes tick up.
